utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning. May we have -- thank you, Madam Registrar. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: May it please the Court, appearing for the Prosecution today, Belinda Pidwell, Alexis Demirdjian, and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Mr. Jason Antley, and Ms. Katarina Danicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm assuming that everything is in place in Sarajevo and we can continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. You may resume your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dzafic. Can you hear me, Mr. Dzafic?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I will be putting a number of questions to you which are, if I may say so, of a general nature given that you have been a policeman for many years, I think since 1977. Therefore, we thought that your experience in that field would be of assistance to us here. Mr. Dzafic, yesterday during examination-in-chief you spoke of check-points which existed in Kljuc municipality in 1991. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The reference is on page 63 and onwards of yesterday's transcript. Sir, isn't it true that in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in 1991, on all the main roads in all municipalities of Bosnia and Herzegovina there were check-points set up?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, do you remember that in the course of 1991 there was an initiative in place called "Check-point 1991," or "Check-point 91"?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember that initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was a joint initiative, a joint campaign of the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the JNA. They had mixed check-points manned by military units, units of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they were set up on certain roads. They mostly dealt with confiscation of illegal weapons and so on. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yesterday when one of the documents was shown to you, the duty roster or something like that, duty log, you commented on a colleague of yours, he was under number 17. I don't want to show you the document now so as not to waste time, but there was an indication, PUK, by his name, or PUV. Then you explained that that stood for "Check-Point Velagic."

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, yesterday you explained that at those check-points, and I think that if I'm not mistaken there were four or five in the territory of Kljuc municipality, the police had a discretion to take some activities or not take them, the policemen who worked at that -- those check-points. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That discretionary right pertained to persons in vehicles who had certain passes. Such persons were not even stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I say a discretionary right, this is the kind of a situation that I have in mind. Let me clarify this for you. Such persons, these persons, policemen who manned those check-points in Kljuc municipality in 1991 and early 1992, policemen who were members of the SJB in Kljuc, had a discretion to stop somebody as they saw fit and let somebody pass. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly like that. They had patrol instructions that they were supposed to implement during their duty shift at the check-point. However, certain vehicles such as JNA vehicles or other vehicles with special designation would be stopped only pro forma, without actually checking the vehicle, without inspecting it, and then they would be let through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, you want to say that the entire traffic on that road passing through that check-point, every vehicle was stopped and some sort of an inspection was conducted; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if vehicles had special passes, the ones that you mentioned, JNA vehicles and the like, they would be let through without inspection, whereas in other cases they would actually inspect.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This inspection encompassed establishing somebody's identity; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, establishing the identity of passengers, a search of luggage, vehicle, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So establishing the identity -- I stopped for the sake of the transcript, Mr. Dzafic. I apologise to you. Sir, both of us need to slow down, because the interpreters need to interpret, and then it needs to be recorded and so on. So when we say establishing the identity, that means that everyone who was in a vehicle was ID'd. They had to show their ID. Plus a driver had to show his papers, papers for the vehicle, his driver's licence, and so on. Am I right in stating this?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then the MUP policemen had to open up the vehicle, open up the trunk, and the purpose of that was to confiscate any illegal weapons or any illegal substances transported in the vehicle; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if they were -- if there were to be somebody in the vehicle without proper IDs, or if they found a controlled substance, illegal substance or an object in the car, then the policemen, in accordance with their authorities under the law, would take up the measures as prescribed in the law; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, tell me, please, you remember that in 1991, pursuant to an order from the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and also an order from the Minister Alija Delimustafic, who was minister of the interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the reserve forces were called up. Reserve police forces were called up. It was in the summer or perhaps September of 1991.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So from that moment on when the reserve police forces were mobilised in the summer or in September of 1991 due to a somewhat deteriorating security situation, the reserve forces remained activated until April of 1992 and onwards.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were activated were almost identical to active police members. They were just as active.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, especially given the period of time during which they were activated.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I think that you will be of great assistance to us in explaining some of the units that you mentioned yesterday on page 52, line 3 and onwards. Yesterday, my learned friend asked you about manoeuvre units and then you explained them. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember well, you said that a manoeuvre unit was composed of younger trained members of the MUP, and there were approximately 60 of them in Kljuc, two platoons, if I remember well, and those are the people that were trained in various specialties, for example, dispersing crowds and other needs. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a manoeuvre unit in Kljuc had about 60 members. In establishment terms, it comprised two platoons, and then each platoon had squads that were specialised in certain areas, and if the unit was engaged in activities in the territory of the unit, it was led by an officer from the Kljuc SJB. And if it was engaged in activities in other municipalities, then the person who would decide on that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that. You said that yesterday. No need to repeat, but I just want to clarify something that hopefully will be of assistance to the Chamber and everybody else. This manoeuvre unit, it existed in plans, didn't it? It had -- it was listed in various documents. All of its members during normal working hours were engaged in their regular duties. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Active policemen - and about 30 per cent of them were members of the manoeuvre unit - once they completed manoeuvre activities would return to their regular police duties; whereas reserve policemen would go back to their companies where they normally worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps the best way to proceed is to provide an example. Let's imagine this, the following situation: There is a football match in Banja Luka. For instance, Zeleznicar and Borac are in the match, and there is an assessment that there might be some riots after the football match. The Banja Luka police station, which is charged with crowd control during this match will then ask for assistance from other police stations in the area because they do not have a sufficient number of men in order to provide security for such an event. At that point the chief or the commander would issue an order, for instance, for a platoon of 30 active policemen, that manoeuvre unit, for instance, to be assigned to Banja Luka and carry out the assignment which would be to provide security during this football match. And in the same manner Kljuc would provide 30 men, Sanski Most 15, Prijedor 12, and so forth. Is this -- is this how it worked?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in other words, they would be assigned there, the football match is over, the entire assignment took some five or six hours, and then they returned to Kljuc, members of this manoeuvre unit. And then once they are back in Kljuc, they would just go back to their normal police work and duties, such as patrolling, duty service and so on. Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Except that the platoon from Kljuc, for instance, that you mentioned would be subordinated to a commanding officer in Banja Luka, and that commanding officer in Banja Luka would then assign -- assign them tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've been very helpful. Now, sir, let us just make a distinction here. The manoeuvre units that we've just described, and I think the description will suffice, they had nothing to do with the special -- with the MUP special brigade from Sarajevo that was under the competence of the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This Special Police Brigade was a special brigade of the ministry at its headquarters, and that brigade had no connections or no ties whatsoever with these manoeuvre units; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really remember exactly, but I think that's about right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think there's another topic where you could be of great assistance to us, and I would like to put a few questions to you about it. Now, you've -- you mentioned yesterday the duty roster and some other logs that were kept as a matter of procedure, standard procedure, at various public security stations, or at least that was the case in 1990 and 1991 and 1992. I apologise. I'm working -- I'm waiting for the transcript to catch up with us. I think we've just got carried away, both you and I. Now one of the logs or records that were kept by the policemen at the duty operations centre at the public security stations was a log-book of daily events; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This log-book or diary which was kept at every security station would contain information and entries for any significant events or incidents that occurred on that particular day in the area of responsibility of that public security station. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That log-book would -- would contain all that, and in addition to the log-book there was also a diary of the duty officer, who would also keep a record of every event that would be reported during his duty shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So we do have a diary and the log-book, the operations officer's log-book; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So these two documents are similar in nature. I suppose that in the log-book -- or in the duty diary the -- the -- there would be more details.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if there was some significant event, it would be described in more detail in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the basis of this diary of all events in the course of a day, at the end of the day there would be a report drafted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the daily information report?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the daily information report that you would be sending to the security services centre every day.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there would be a daily report for the past 24 hours, and it would be forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that daily information report would be based on the diary and log-book for the previous day.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. That report would contain all the significant events that had to do with disturbances, public -- law and order, any traffic incidents and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And every morning, as a rule, this report would be sent, the report for the previous day. It would be sent in the morning to the security services centre; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me this: This daily report would be submitted in written form as a dispatch, and it would be sent via teleprinter; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really recall, but it was standard to send it. It was standard procedure to send it as a dispatch, but I can't really recall clearly. And if there was an emergency, then there would also be reports made over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the phone line or phone communication was only used in emergencies; correct? As a rule, the daily report was sent in writing; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because obviously by phone it would be impossible to relate everything in such detail as you would be able to do it in a written report, correct, in a dispatch?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dzafic. Thank you very much. I have no further questions for you. Have a good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dzafic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Krgovic, and I am on the Defence team of Stojan Zupljanin. I will have a few questions for you that relate to your prior testimony and the statement that you provided to the investigator of this Tribunal. Since we both speak the same language, and I tend to speed up when I speak, please make a pause between my question and your answer, although I see that you already observe that, because this will help our interpreters to do a better job.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Dzafic, if I understood you correctly, in 1991 -- or, rather, from 1990 up until the -- all the changes that happened after the multi-party elections, you were the commander of the police station in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since 1977 up until 1991, I was appointed first as the deputy commander and then commander, and then after the elections I had to -- I was appointed chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And at one point in time after the elections, up until Vinko Kondic was appointed, you actually were the acting chief of the public security station in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in that capacity as acting chief, you had occasion to meet with Zupljanin in Banja Luka when you attended these regular monthly meetings in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, even before I was appointed as acting chief, while I was still the commander, I met and attended these regular -- I met with Mr. Zupljanin and attended these regular meetings in Banja Luka; whereas during my capacity as acting chief, I believe there were just one or two such occasions, one or two such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And once Vinko Kondic was appointed chief, you no longer attended those meetings in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now describe the chain of command, as it were, the police chain of command, as a commander, "komandir" in B/C/S. In addition to your duties and responsibilities toward the chief, you also had certain duties in the police structure as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the territory of the municipality there were various public security stations. The next level was the security services centre, and the third level, the top level, was the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So in that -- within that structure at the public security station you had occasion to communicate with Stevan Markovic at the CSB in Banja Luka, who was in charge of those duties; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then the next one up the chain was the chief of the sector of the public security stations, Jahic Bajazit, who was at the Banja Luka CSB; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, but if that's what it says in the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And along -- or up that police chain of command, the public security chain of command, you also had occasion to go to Sarajevo, and the person who would be your superior there was Cedo Kljajic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really recall, but I know that before the multi-party elections we had -- or I had, as the commander, we were inspected or inspections were conduct by some inspectors from Sarajevo. They would review our work and review my work as a commander, a sort of supervisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But as a matter of principle, in addition to this chain of command you were also responsible or you also answered to the chief of the public security station, Vinko Kondic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. He was my immediate superior at the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you were issued or sent a communication from Markovic that differed from the order or assignment issued by Vinko Kondic, you would actually have to abide by Vinko Kondic's order or obey his order; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would depend on the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for instance, if you were issued an order to carry out a check somewhere or an inspection and you were issued this order by Vinko Markovic -- by Markovic and Vinko Kondic were to tell you not to -- that you didn't have to do that, you wouldn't do it; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they wouldn't really issue contradictory commands. However, toward of end of 1991 and in early 1992, there were some contradictory orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then what would your duty be? What was it that you would have to carry out, whose orders?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to discuss this with Chief Kondic, and then we would agree on what it was that we would have to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And his would be the final decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, in your statement you described the appointment of Stojan Zupljanin as chief of the security services centre. That's on page 4 of your statement. You have it before you. That's under tab 1 in the binder, and the 65 ter number is 9016. That's in the OTP binder, whereas in the e-court -- Witness, would you please take a look at page 4. The ERN number is 007113. That's page 3 in the English. 007113. So you've found that, I suppose. There it says before the -- prior to the multi-party elections, Stojan Zupljanin was the chief of the crime police of the municipal SUP for Banja Luka, and then as chief of the municipal SUP in Banja Luka. He was then appointed the chief of the CSB for Banja Luka region after three other candidates turned down the appointment offers. Just a brief clarification here. Was it standard practice, both in the case of your appointment and in this case, that a number of candidates be proposed for a certain post within the police force?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the case with you as well; is that correct? There were several candidates who were proposed for your post?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, there were two other candidates for my post, in addition to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And now if I were to tell you that in addition to Zupljanin, for this post there were a number of candidates, is that how I am to read this statement of yours? Perhaps I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't get you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when Stojan Zupljanin was appointed as chief of the CSB, there were a number of other appointee -- a number of other candidates for that post. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I learned from one candidate personally that he declined the offer. He was formally placed on the list as a candidate, but he was not prepared to actually take the post. If you'd like me to, I can give you his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We can go into private session if you wish.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was chief of the criminal investigation police for Banja Luka region.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, is this terribly relevant or important?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I just wanted to clarify something from the statement, because reading the statement, it would appear that everyone else turned down the offer and that that's why Stojan Zupljanin was appointed. That's all I wanted to clarify, and I'm moving to more important topics. This was just a minor one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, in your statement you described this procedure on signing the solemn declaration by which the policemen would accept or decline loyalty to the authorities. You said that mostly all Muslims rejected to sign this declaration except for one Croat. Do you remember mentioning that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. In a meeting, there were active policemen present from Kljuc who were non-Serbs, and mostly all of them refused to sign loyalty to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Except for Zdeno Modric. You mentioned him; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zdeno Modric whose parents were of two different ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And Alija Salihovic; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that name. I don't think there is a policeman called Alija Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He used to play handball.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Salihovic was a reserve policeman, not an active one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he accepted to remain in the police of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I hear it for the first time now. I know Mr. Alija Salihovic personally. He teaches physical education.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, at one point in time after your arrest you were taken to the school in Sitnica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion an officer told you as you arrived that you would be transferred to Manjaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the same day, just prior to our departure for Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he said to you that you would be escorted by military police; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. He said that we would be escorted and that nobody should dare to escape or do anything else, otherwise they would use weapons, since we went from Sitnica to Manjaca on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will remind you of that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the addendum to the statement, 65 ter 10247. This is from the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, while we're waiting, it's the addendum where you corrected certain things and you described precisely this event. So I wanted to refresh your memory concerning it.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's tab 3 of this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said tab 3. It wasn't recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, please look at paragraph 7 of this statement, where you say: "He told me we would be escorted by the military police and that I and other Muslim policemen, and there were approximately five of us, should place ourselves along the entire convoy." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the words of that person, security person, who told me that, but that's not how it was. He told this to me in the office in the gym at Sitnica. He said to me that this -- this morning as we were about to go on foot from Sitnica to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then at some point in time you set out in a column to Manjaca; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the morning, at around 10.00, we were lined up in front of the gym, and we were in a long column, five of us in a row. We had our hands behind our heads. We had to face the ground, and we started out on foot towards Manjaca. On both sides of our column were members of reserve police forces of the reserve police branch office in Sitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in front of you --

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind us there was a vehicle. I was quite beaten up. I was in terrible pain, and I was somewhere in the beginning of the column. There was a vehicle travelling behind us. It could have been a minibus or a van. I can't remember now. At any rate, the vehicle was for the persons who couldn't walk. Those people would be put in that vehicle and transported together with us to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this military officer who told you that --

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that military officer was in his vehicle, and he travelled in front of us, quite ahead, quite a lot ahead of us in order to secure unhindered passage for us, because there were local residents in various settlements. For example, in Kadina Voda where we rested and where we were given some water. Local residents gathered there, and they wanted to shoot at us, and this military officer dispersed those crowds. That's why he travelled in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he was travelling in a passenger vehicle, in his passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I know that that military officer wore a military uniform, a camouflage multicoloured uniform, and he introduced himself to us as a security person. He had a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead. I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was a captain or perhaps a lieutenant. He had two or three stars. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he escorted you to Manjaca, to the location where you were handed over.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And along the road you stopped twice, if I understood you well, to have some water.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there were just natural sources with jerry cans next to them to enable you to drink water; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were natural sources, and the locals would bring their buckets and jerry cans, the ones that they used in their households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sitnica, from which you started out, it is outside of Kljuc on the very edge of Manjaca; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sitnica is a local commune within Kljuc municipality. The last one bordering with Banja Luka and Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you think that it's 10 to 15 kilometres away, right, this place where you set out from to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me explain it to you. From Sitnica, from the gym in Sitnica to Manjaca there is some 10 or so kilometres. That road was very long for us given our exhaustion and general condition that we were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I looked at your CV, and it appears that you graduated from the school for reserve officers in Zadar; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I graduated from the school for reserve officers in Zadar as an artillery man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During your training there, were you instructed in how to escort prisoners of war? Were you given any instruction in provisions on escorting prisoners of war, namely, that they could be transported on foot, in trucks, by train, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. The training that we had at the school for reserve officers was eight months long. We were mostly taught military subjects. We had to learn a lot. So that's what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't recorded in the transcript. You said, "More or less I was familiar with that"; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, as an officer, do you know that when combat operations are carried out -- and naturally you as policemen must have participated in some military exercises in the old Yugoslavia; right? And then when these military operations are conducted and police forces participate in it, then they are resubordinated to the military in that operation; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no military exercises with combat operations. However, I am familiar, from the command and control system, with that principle, that if a number of units are participating, then some units are subordinated to some other units within this command and control system. They are subordinated to the unit in charge of that particular exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, the Prosecutor asked you and showed you a document, and I would like you to look at it now. This is 23 in the OTP binder. Tab 23. 791 is the number on the 65 ter list. You have the document before you; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it yesterday for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph it says that the weapons relocated because there is a serious threat that the Green Berets could attack the depot where the weapons are held, and as far as you know, this is not true. There was no looming danger, no threat; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday Vrhpolje is in Sanski Most municipality. As for Velagici, I had no such information that there was a risk, that there was a danger that members of the Green Berets would attack the police station. I had no such information as long as I was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So according to you, the information in this document is not correct; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then in Velagici, where it says that the greatest number of risk is posed by Green Berets from Velagici, that is not true either; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were a lot of guards set up in many locations. The residents of Velagici were predominantly Muslim. It is just a local commune, and this information here that there were 12.500 inhabitants is really exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this entire report is not reliable; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, this intelligence report is not reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dzafic. Yesterday, in reply to questions put to you by the Prosecutor, you spoke of a unit of Red Berets who had come to Kljuc in order to restore law and order -- or, rather, to deal mostly with the military conscripts who would cause disorder when coming back from the front. I want to clarify that those were military persons. These members of the Red Berets, they were from the 5th Military Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who they were and to which army they belonged, but we in Kljuc considered them to be Green Berets, about a dozen of them, not more than that. And at that time in Kljuc there were numerous disruptions of law and order by soldiers who would come back home from the front and cause disorder in various pubs and cafes and so on. So these members would assist regular police officers in -- in conducting regular police activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, a correction for the transcript. I think it was a slip of the tongue. You said Green Berets, whereas you must have meant Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I meant Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, in 1995, after the forces of the Muslim/Croat federation entered Kljuc, at one point in time you returned to Kljuc and you were appointed as the chief of public -- of the public security station in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was on the 1st of February, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On this occasion, if I understood your testimony correctly, in the safe box in Kljuc you found a certain number of documents that related to -- from 1992 to 1995, documents of the public security station and the Crisis Staff for those years; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were documents that we found in a safe box which we had to open by force because we didn't have a key. We had to use a special device. And in the safe box we found those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I apologise for interrupting you, but there is some confusion, at least in the transcript, regarding the answer that the witness gave to your question just a while ago about the identity of this unit of Red Berets that came to help out, to restore law and order in conclusive. You suggested to the witness that they were part of the 5th Military Corps, and the answer that was given by the witness never really clarified whether this unit was under the control of the JNA or under the control of the MUP. Could you please clarify this issue, because I think that was the purpose of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, this platoon -- or, rather, this squad that dealt with these conscripts who created disturbances, do you know under whose role they were? Were they under military control, under the Territorial Defence or was it some other force?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they provide -- they were regularly on duty on the premises of the TO, so I infer from that that they were under the control of the TO or that they came upon a summons by the commander of the TO, and they spent most of their time there, but from time to time they would also take part in active policing in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I apologise, but let us go back to our earlier topic. Now, you know that once the Muslim/Croat federation forces entered Kljuc some documents were filed, that the AID actually seized these documents and then forwarded them to this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to review these documents during your interview with the Prosecution? Were you shown some of these documents?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was shown some of those documents. There were reports there, and I have to state this, that the 5th Corps units entered Kljuc. They were the first units who entered Kljuc, and they also seized some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Those documents were later forwarded to the Prosecutor, correct, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I would now like to show you one of those documents, and I will need your assistance with it. That is the document under tab 10 in the OTP binder, and it is marked as 2D1000. That's in the Defence binder, not the Prosecutor's binder. I apologise. Mr. Dzafic, would you take a look at this first page. It says there the document's in writing that we found in Kljuc SJB, and the same document was found during the mop-up operation in Kljuc. It speaks of disarming of the guards in villages, their arrest and transfer to Manjaca, a concentration camp. This is a note that was, I assume, drafted not by someone from Republika Srpska but, rather, from the people who actually found these documents. Would you agree with me? I mean, we can infer that from the manner in which this document was drafted.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I see this. I can't really comment on it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, here's my question, then. You said in your statement that an acquaintance told you that when the Serbian Crisis Staff was formed, was established, there was talk about a Muslim Crisis Staff being formed as well and that there would be a meeting to that effect. However, that meeting was never held because the person who was supposed to come to this meeting never showed up. Do you recall talking about this?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This conversation was conducted in Sanica municipal -- in Sanica -- in Sanica area. One of my ex-teachers told me that a Serbian Crisis Staff had been established in Sanica and that there should be a Muslim Crisis Staff also established there in Sanica, whose president would be the village elder. However, that person never showed up, nor was that Crisis Staff ever established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now I have another question. Would you please turn to the next page of this document. We see some names there. The ERN number is 0034-9549.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Here we see some names. Under number 1 we see the name of Muhamed Filipovic. Did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it's Omer Filipovic under number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Just look up at the very beginning of the list.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So there we see the name of Muhamed Filipovic. Did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the SDA; correct? If you know.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The next person is Omer Filipovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You knew him too?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also knew Asim Egrlic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As well as Iksan Zukanovic?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So basically all these individuals under numbers 1 through 6 and then in the next paragraph, 1 to 4, you knew all these people; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know from the first list the person under number 5; and on the second list, I didn't know the individual under number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's Nevzad Djeric; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now please turn a page, go to the next page, and there it says, "The Velagici Company." Let me ask you about these individuals. This first person, is that Ekrem Cekic or Cehic?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Ekrem Cehic. I don't know this person. I had no information whatsoever about the military units that we see here on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this person Salihovic Salih was detained at Manjaca together with you, correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a Salihovic, but I don't know whether his first name was Salih or whether this could have been a different person. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Mustafic person, Ismet Mustafic from Krasulje, was he at Manjaca with you?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Muratovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Muratovic or Muratagic. I can't really tell. It's not clear. The handwriting is unclear.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this person from Manjaca, but you can check the list of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were people from Prhovo detained with you at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the people from Prhovo for the first time while we were detained at the gym in Sitnica. They were brought in. They had been badly beaten, and they were put in the same gym where I was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 3 of this document where it says that some people -- I don't know if this is Cazo Medanovic. It says Prhovo. That's under number 6. The name of Cazim Medanovic appears, and then next to it says "prison."

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says "Cazim Medanovic, prison."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing him?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Or in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that he was imprisoned, because next to his name we see the word "prison."

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just add something here? You see, because of the number of people who were held in these gyms up until the time when we were transferred to Manjaca, and this was a long time ago so I can't really recall every name and last name, there were people called Medanovic, but whether it was Cazim or someone else, I can't really tell with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now please move to the last page of this document and take a look at this last paragraph that reads: "The following police officers were detained: Atif Dzafic, commander." That is a reference to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then it says Mehmedalija Husic; correct? If my reading of this is correct.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mehmedalija Husic, he was a police officer; Resid Omerovic, police officer; Atif Dedic, police officer; Suad Medic, police officer; and Hamdija Kumalic, police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And they were detained together with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't what this here actually refers to. If this is a reference to Manjaca, then yes, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I please -- I move to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is an objection on this. It's a handwritten document which the witness says he hasn't seen before. He doesn't know who wrote it, and all he can do is verify that people on that list were with him in Manjaca. But what I anticipate the Defence want the inference to be taken is -- from Your Honours is that the -- their position such as the -- the descriptions of their vocations next to their names is -- is what is going to be relied upon, and this witness hasn't made any comment about that, and if that is going to be the intention, I'd ask that he be given the opportunity to -- to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would appeal to the Trial Chamber to apply the same standard that was applied yesterday when documents were tendered by the Prosecution. I showed the names of these individuals to the witness. I showed him the places where they had come from, and I asked him whether they were there with him, by which I wanted to demonstrate -- or let me just say this is a document that we actually received from the Prosecution. So would you please apply the same standard that was applied yesterday when the Prosecution documents were being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, before we rule on this issue could you enlighten us as to the provenance of the document? Who -- who drafted this document? When and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document was drafted by the police who conducted an investigation. It was found when the Muslim/Croat federation forces entered Kljuc, and we received this document from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do we have any idea as to who actually wrote this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was written by the investigator who conducted the investigation into the arming. In other words, the person who investigated the individuals who were detained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the investigator wrote this down, but did -- he did so after an interview with someone or -- where does the information come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you look at page 2 of this document, it was drafted on the 10th of June, 1992, after the interviews conducted with most of these individuals. The document comes from the public security station in Kljuc where it was seized. It was seized by the police of the Bosnia-Herzegovina federation when they entered Kljuc in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So if I'm -- just make sure that I understand this correctly. There was in June 1992 an investigation made as to, among other things, the persons who were sent off to Manjaca, and during this investigation one of the investigators took down these notes, and these notes were then later found at the SJB. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, just if I may add. The document has the date of the 10th of June on it, and my learned friend has said that interviews were conducted with the individuals named in this document. Now, the previous witness for the Prosecution and this witness for the Prosecution were both named in this document. There's no evidence before Your Honours that interviews were conduct by an investigator at this time, and so I'm just wondering where my learned friend has that information from and whether evidence is going to be tendered to support his submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will come to that. My next document would be one of the statements taken by investigators, Your Honours. So could we show to the witness tab -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, taking Ms. Pidwell's question, we would agree to the document being exhibited at this point with the understanding that it is for the limited purpose of it being a document which the witness has testified to, that he recognises some of the names on it, but any inferences that you would wish the Chamber to draw further than that, there would need to be more evidence. So we would have it marked and admitted at this stage subject to that limitation, with that understanding.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit will be given number 2D44.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 2D02-100 -- I apologise. 2D06-0510, and that's tab 53 in the Defence binder, and it is in reference to the objection raised just now by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify that. Mr. Dzafic, before this document is shown to you, when you worked at the police, the standard procedure was that when somebody was brought into the police station, the police would interview that person and draft a statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in that initial procedure that person would give that statement either in the status of a citizen or in the status of a suspect; right? Depending on the assessment of the person interviewing him or her; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then the person giving the statement would sign the statement and initial each page of the statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at the statement before you. Please tell me, did you know Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The form of the statement is a typical one, isn't it? This is what statements normally look like taken in the regular standard procedure by the police?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at first glance it appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at all the pages and the last page of this document. You see that it is signed. Please look carefully at all of the pages and you will see that there is an identical signature on each page. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the last page -- or, rather, the penultimate page -- first of, all, do you know that Omer Filipovic was appointed commander of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have that information that he was appointed commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then this last paragraph, read it carefully, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I was about to invite you when you reach a suitable point and we would take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you please read this paragraph and then this portion where you are mentioned, the last sentence. "I believed that Atif Dzafic, whom I didn't contact and who doesn't know about this, should be in the internal affairs due to his expertise." So nobody contacted you, telling you that you needed to be appointed to this position within the Ministry of the Interior? You didn't know about this?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew about that. I'm really surprised to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this sentence is correct. He never told you that you had been planned for that position; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: There is an objection on that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it has to do with the objection by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is a statement made by a man that the witness does know or did know, but the witness is no longer alive and we have no evidence as to the circumstances of surrounding when or where or how this statement was taken, and there's no evidence to support any of the surrounding circumstances. If it's tendered simply as an example of a statement taken with the limitation that -- the limitation of the portion that Mr. Krgovic has put to this witness about himself, then I would submit it be tendered simply with that caveat attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may reply briefly. If you look at the last page, it will describe the circumstances under which the statement is taken. "I have no complaints against the authorised officials who took this statement from me because they applied correct procedure." We received this document from the Prosecution and in order to avoid making a motion under 92 quater, I wish to tender the statement into evidence, because I think that if you apply the same standard that you applied yesterday, when the Prosecution tendered a huge number of documents through this witness, then I think you should do the same today. And the witness confirmed that this statement was signed and that it was taken in accordance with the procedure in force at the time. And he also confirmed the accuracy of the information in this statement. So I think that this is sufficient grounds for admitting it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, accepting the very last statement you made about confirming the accuracy of the information, wouldn't it be -- this would probably be better addressed to Ms. Pidwell. Wouldn't the simpler course to be at this point to have it admitted as a fact with the truth to be developed as -- as we go along. Going back to first principles and distinguishing the fact of the statement from the truth of the statement. Wouldn't that be the simpler course?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it's admitted on the basis that a statement was taken from this witness, on this date, in this manner, then absolutely I agree with Your Honours on that basis. The truth of the contents is another matter, and if my learned friend is asking for the Trial Chamber to adopt the accuracy of the information in the report, my submission would be you can only adopt the accuracy of the information if it is put to this witness as was that one small portion that -- that has -- was put to him in prior -- prior, and that was the caveat that I referred to previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Your response, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Trial Chamber did not have such a caveat when admitting Prosecution documents yesterday. I can look into more facts in the statement with this witness so as to have him confirm that the events described here are accurate. I just wanted to apply the abbreviated procedure. And naturally with other witnesses we will be discussing contents of this statement. We will be showing it to other witnesses as well. I simply believe this to be the first step in establishing the events which -- and facts which took place in Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, it isn't particularly helpful for you to remind the Chamber that it should apply the same standards as it did previous, because the Chamber has to make a decision in respect of each application, and as I recall, the Prosecution's yesterday went in in terms of a package and I don't recall there being any objection by the Defence in terms of specific items in that package. So that particular line isn't helpful. But the -- holding you to what you have represented that you would be able to do, it seems to me that the -- that the document would be admissible with that caveat. So it's admitted and marked, and we are pastime for the break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number 2D45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just owe an explanation. My client has cap on his head because he has a cold and there is an air-conditioning opening right above his head, so he's wearing a cap to protect himself, and this is the reason for his athletic appearance today. We asked for him to be given cold medication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Krgovic. That has been explained to us, and you can -- I would say to you in the presence of your client, who I assume understand -- can hear me directly, that if he feels unwell at any time he can indicate it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, and another explanation. Perhaps I used a wrong term. It was not my intention to admonish the Trial Chamber. I used a formulation that wasn't precise enough, so I apologise to you for doing that. It was just before the break when we were discussing the issue of admitting this document into evidence. I awkwardly expressed myself, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, you explained to the Prosecution and also in your statement the events that preceded your arrest, so I would like to go with you briefly over those events. Can you please tell me -- or, rather, would you agree with me that the first conflict that was more serious took place in Kljuc when Deputy Commander Stojakovic was killed in Krasulje in May of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day when the deputy commander, Mr. Stojakovic, lost his life in Krasulje, I was in Sanica. It wasn't until several days later that I learned of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's how I understood your testimony. However, you heard that there was shooting at the entry point into Krasulje, that an armed Muslim group opened fire on the passing vehicles as a result of which Stojakovic was killed and several policemen were wounded. Did you hear of this subsequently?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard subsequently several versions of that incident. I did not investigate it myself, nor did I engage in the investigation process, but there are several versions, one of which is the one you just told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when the shooting was over, the people who were wounded and who were in the vicinity were picked up by the Kljuc police. Do you know anything about it? And that Omer Filipovic participated --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would object to him continuing with this line of questioning as the witness has said that he heard various versions of this event. At this time, he wasn't -- he had been dismissed from the Kljuc police command and was in Sanica, so any information that he has is, by his own admission, hearsay. And there are various versions out there, none of which he knows which one is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, how does having regard --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since hearsay is admitted here, the witness referred to hearsay information numerous times in examination-in-chief. So my line of questioning when asking about Omer Filipovic was aimed in that direction. Who told him, when -- when they told him that. Fifty per cent of the statement that was admitted is based on hearsay. I need to verify with the witness what he heard, from whom, and what was his role in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Except that the narrow question of hearsay apart, the gravamen of Ms. Pidwell's objection is that what the witness has said so far is that he wasn't present. There were a variety of versions, and he is in no position to testify to the accuracy or truth of one as opposed to the other. That is what I understand the objection to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will get to that. I will clarify that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I apologise for this minor confusion. When you were at Manjaca, you were there with Omer Filipovic, and you used to see him there; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't with Omer Filipovic. Omer Filipovic was in the last -- in the third stable, and I was in the second stable at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see him?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally when we went to have our meals, until he was placed in a solitary confinement cell, the one that we described that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss these events?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the event when the convoy in Busija was attacked, you learned of it one or two hours later from Dragan Tomic, a squad commander.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I had spent several days in Sanica with my family, I was about to return to Kljuc, and on that very day I was informed -- or, rather, since I had information that the road between Velagici and Sanica was blocked, I met up with the commander of the police squad in Sanica, and he told me about the convoy and that the road was blocked and that there was no movement until further notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, you will agree with me that all the way up until the 26th or 27th of May, when these incidents took place and when policeman Stojakovic was killed and when the military convoy in Busija was attacked, there were no conflicts in the territory of Kljuc municipality?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some individual killings previously. There was a killing in Sanica and one in the centre of Kljuc. However, these two incidents were more pronounced than the previous events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This incident that you spoke about in the centre of Kljuc, that was sometime in April or early 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know that in the centre of Kljuc, at an intersection, Dervisevic was killed, a citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Dervisevic, Senad; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was killed by a military conscript of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was killed by a soldier called Boro Grujicic, from Sitnica; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. Boro Grujicic from Sitnica. And previously there was a killing in Sanica. Admir Selmanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, you must have heard this. The two of us understand each other, and I will do my best not to interrupt you when you're speaking. So this event, when Senad Dervisevic was killed, that killing was resolved, and it was investigated by an inspector called Muharem Musovic [as interpreted], called Muki; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he was arrested, but since he was a military person he was taken over by the military police from Banja Luka who took them with him; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you said it was in late 1991, early 1992. Roughly in that period of time; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And for the other crime you mentioned in Sanica, the same inspector, Muharem Muheljic investigated this other crime as well, but the perpetrator was never found; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An investigation was conducted. A number of persons were suspected of this crime, but ultimately the perpetrator was never identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And following that, following these tensions and problems with reservists in Kljuc municipality, until the ambushes there were no armed incidents of greater significance as far as you know; right?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that actually signified the beginning of the conflict in Kljuc or the beginning of combat operations, if we can call them that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 27th of May, following which the well-known events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We know about that. Mr. Dzafic, the Prosecutor, when you spoke about exhumation, you spoke about the event at the school in Velagici when a large number of Muslims were killed. You know about that event, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that event because on that very day, on the 1st of June, I took a detour road -- rather, I was brought via a detour road with a number of other citizens to there, and we had passed by the check-point in Velagici in the vicinity of which there was an elementary school where they kept Muslims from the territory of Velagici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned seeing a Serb soldier on that road. You mentioned his name, and you said that he was in a military uniform; right? I can't remember whom you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the first bus and there were a total of three. We were escorted by active policemen and reservists. There were two policemen on each bus. We couldn't see much because we had been ordered to keep our hands behind our backs and to stare at the floor, and the curtains were drawn on the windows of the bus. But as far as I could remember, at the check-point in Velagici there was a mixed composition of active and reserve police and military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, you have a --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I wonder if we could have a reference please. The question was you mentioned his name, you saw a Serb soldier on the road in military uniform. I can't remember whom you mentioned. I don't know where -- don't recall that coming out of evidence in-chief and I'm just wondering where the reference came from in his statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I remember reading this in one of the documents. The witness did mention that, but I can't find the reference right now. So I just asked him if he could recall the name of that person without actually me refreshing his memory.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I mentioned a person. He was a salesperson of Serb ethnicity. As we took the forest road towards Velagici, I believe his name was Dragoja. Is that the person you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly at the check-point at Velagici.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. This was at the check-point before Velagici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I think I misunderstood your statement. Now let's go back to the incident in Velagici or around Velagici. You said that you had heard about this innocent when you were in Velagici; correct? In Velagici. That was on the 1st of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I passed through that check-point sometime in the afternoon, and -- but while I was still in the stable, a person from Velagici came into our stable, a person who had been detained at the school and who had actually managed to survive an execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like now to show you 2D42. That's already an exhibit. And that will be under tab 55 in the Defence binder. Could you please read this. This is a report or a request to conduct an investigation of an individual. And then if you turn the page you will see -- look at the part which says: "Because of a ground of suspicion that," et cetera, et cetera. So could you please read this paragraph. Does this deal with the incident that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a description of the incident that I learned of later on when I was at Manjaca from this person, Mr. Draganovic. I can't really recall his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the individuals mentioned here. Do you know or do you recognise any of these names? Most of these were military persons.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recognise the person under number 3, Bosko Uncanin. He was from Sanica, a neighbour. I also recognise Zoran Banjac under number 8. And as for the rest, I see that they were conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These two were conscripts, as far as I can see here.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. I'm a little bit at a loss. I can't find the document in the documents that were sent to us, and the one that's on the screen appears to be the statement that was previously tendered being -- it's just Mr. Filipovic's statement. Perhaps Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D42. I apologise. Maybe the interpreters did not hear me well. That's 2D42. This was tendered and admitted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I apologise. You can see that this deals with the crime committed in Velagici, and that they were 12 individuals who were interviewed as suspects and charged. There was a request submitted for an investigation to be conducted of these persons who were suspected of having committed this crime, and it was suspected that these conscript -- conscripts had actually committed that murder in Velagici.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this request for an investigation, that's what it would seem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Another question. Yesterday when you were -- during the examination-in-chief you mentioned the exhumation in Biljani. I'm referring to an incident sometime in June 1992. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. On the 10th of July. Now, you learned of this subsequently at Manjaca or --

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of that at Manjaca, and after the war I was able to ascertain this in person during the exhumation at Laniste 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would now like to show you a document that relates to that indent. Could we see document 65 ter 814. And in your binder it's under tab 48. This document bears the number -- ERN number 65 ter 814964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Mr. Krgovic, I understand this document is not in the witness's binder so he will have to see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
